title: serratula lycopifolia
intro: Serratula lycopifolia, commonly known as Indian teaberry or Indian sage, is a plant species native to the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia. It has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever, cough, and respiratory problems, due to its health benefits, which include its expectorant and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Serratula lycopifolia include its ability to relieve congestion, reduce fever, and soothe respiratory tract irritations. Bioactive constituents present in the plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
